instructions: Create a separate checkout/worktree at the exact native revision; never apply this patch to shipping sources.
Apply studio-amd560x-scalar-20261106.patch to that isolated checkout.

Configure Release with GGML_METAL=ON GGML_METAL_EMBED_LIBRARY=ON GGML_NATIVE=OFF GGML_AVX=ON GGML_AVX2=ON GGML_FMA=ON GGML_F16C=ON GGML_OPENMP=OFF GGML_BLAS=ON GGML_BLAS_VENDOR=Apple BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF LLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON LLAMA_BUILD_UI=OFF LLAMA_CURL=OFF LLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF.
Build test-backend-ops and llama-completion only with bounded parallelism.
Run MESHLIT_AMD_SCALAR_PROBE=1 test-backend-ops test -b MTL0 -o MUL_MAT -p <exact filter above>; require executed nonzero tests, not skipped output.

Run llama-completion with verified starter weights, the exact prompt above, -n 8 -c 512 -b 32 -ub 32 -t 4 --temp 0 --seed 42 --no-conversation --no-display-prompt --ignore-eos --verbose --no-kv-offload --flash-attn off. CPU adds -ngl 0 --device none --no-op-offload; candidate adds -ngl 4 --device MTL0 and the opt-in environment.
Keep default warmup enabled for the recorded reproducible positive test.

decision: Do not promote: arithmetic sanity and selected numeric equality passed, but scalar AMD decode is about fifteen times slower in this short probe. CPU remains default. A useful AMD engine needs optimized wave64-safe kernels and fewer CPU/GPU transfers, followed by broader correctness, cancellation, memory/thermal and repeated workload measurements.
hyperlBoundary: Meshlit embedded HyperL recipes are separate. Standalone HyperL-plan has CPU/RPC GGUF adapter proof; no AMD LLM acceleration qualification is inferred from it.
